# Redis

Driving Redis as a data-structure server — the craft that separates a cache from a Swiss-army engine.

- **Pick the structure by the job, not habit:** string for blobs/flags · hash for object-shaped fields mutated independently (`HSET user:1 name`) · set for membership/dedup · sorted set for rankings, sliding windows, and time-indexed sweeps · list for simple queues · streams for consumer-group work distribution — a JSON blob in a string that gets read-modify-written per field wanted to be a hash.
- **Atomicity is the whole point:** `INCR`/`DECR`, `SETNX`, `HINCRBY`, `ZADD` — one command, one atomic step; anything multi-step that must be atomic is a short Lua script (the limiter check, the token-bucket refill, the lock takeover) — read-then-write from the app is a race with extra steps.
- **TTL discipline is memory management:** every key expires unless a named reason says otherwise; `EXPIRE` rides the same script/pipeline as the write — a keyspace where `DBSIZE` only grows is a leak wearing a dashboard. Eviction policy chosen deliberately per instance: `noeviction` for queues/locks (losing them is corruption), `allkeys-lru`/`lfu` for pure cache pools.
- **Split by concern, not by luck:** logical DBs (or separate instances) for cache / queue / locks / rate-limit / sessions — one `FLUSHDB` of the cache must never eat the queue; eviction tuned per concern becomes possible; the blast radius of a hot instance stays named.
- **`KEYS` never, `SCAN` always** — and pattern-scans are an admin operation, not a request path; a request that needs to enumerate keys is a data model asking for a set/zset index of its members.
- **Pipeline the multi-key beats:** N round-trips collapse into one pipeline; Lua when the steps depend on each other — the hot path budget is round-trips first, payload second.
- **Big keys and hot keys are the two production killers:** a multi-MB value blocks the single-threaded loop for everyone (cap value sizes, chunk collections); one celebrity key concentrating traffic melts a cluster shard (localize with L1, or shard the key by suffix). Hunt both with `redis-cli --bigkeys` / latency monitoring on a schedule.
- **Locks done honestly:** `SET key token NX PX ttl` + delete-by-token via Lua (never delete a lock you no longer own); TTL sized to the critical section with margin; a lock without a TTL is a deadlock with paperwork. Distributed-lock heroics beyond this (multi-node consensus) mean the design wants a different tool.
- **Persistence matches the concern:** cache pools can lose everything (no persistence, fast restarts) · queues/locks want AOF `everysec` — and either way the app treats Redis loss as a survivable event with a warm-up story, never a data-loss incident.
- Know the single-threaded contract: commands are cheap but serial — an O(N) command on a big structure (`SMEMBERS`, `LRANGE 0 -1`, fat `ZRANGE`) stalls every caller; paginate with cursors and ranges, and watch `SLOWLOG` like a query log.
